quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: Can complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, its rear wheels follow a shorter path than its front wheels. Long trucks have a bigger difference between these paths. Because of this, large trucks often need to swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. You should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: When merging, you need to find a gap that is large enough for you to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps available.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the roadway, but an oncoming vehicle is approaching. You should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time when possible. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then you can pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating a hazard. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle merges too close in front of you, take your foot off the accelerator. This creates space between you and the vehicle ahead without hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead makes a very sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a very sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns drivers to slow down and prepare for a sharp change in road direction.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers making a left turn must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing where they should not, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns drivers of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: A red painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your driving lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror before returning to your lane. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the lane nearest the right curb, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before you turn. Slow down and move into the right lane. Stay as close as possible to the right curb before turning.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can reduce your ability to drive safely. Mixing them with alcohol is especially dangerous.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the edge of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
Turn back onto the roadway immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back immediately. Reduce speed, check traffic, and gradually turn back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; curving road ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: You see a green traffic light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can completely cross the intersection.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can completely cross the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can completely cross before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto the freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of existing traffic.

questions.question: When leaving a parked spot at a curb to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the speed of other traffic.

questions.question: When may you pass a vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Paying attention to your surroundings and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions are common causes of crashes. Always drive at safe speeds within the legal limit.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: You should not assume you have the right-of-way. Always look at what is happening at an intersection. Be ready to yield if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: It is illegal to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not cross the centerline to pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far ahead. Never pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, or where a solid yellow line is next to your lane. Do not pass when the car in front has stopped for a pedestrian or in construction zones.

questions.question: If you are in a crash, you should:

options.text: Move injured people far away from the road.
Do not move injured people unless absolutely necessary.
Tell injured people they are fine and do not need medical help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move injured people unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people. Only move them if there is fire or other immediate danger. Keep injured people sitting or lying down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or road edge.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn away from the curb.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
Do not have to follow traffic rules.
Must always yield to motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers should respect bicyclists' rights on the road.

questions.question: You are in a minor crash with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Never move your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.
Brake firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning. If it happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You can turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before turning.
Traffic moves to the right.
Traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, unless a sign says you cannot. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if you cannot keep your eyes open, drift between lanes, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake. When you notice these signs, park safely and rest with a short nap.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is difficult because of low visibility. You cannot judge the distance to other vehicles or how fast they are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reactions slower and less reliable.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no traffic from either direction can cross the center line to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that tells drivers traffic laws. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with traffic moving counterclockwise around a center island. It has no traffic signal. When entering, yield to cars already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right and exit onto your road.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas. Do not brake hard. Let the car slow down by itself. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they do not show the area directly behind your car. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use only your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Use only your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Watch traffic in front of you and in the lane next to you.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase the risk of a crash.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky driving choices.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of crashes. Driving too fast does not save time. It often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane of a two-lane road. Many cars are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for passing and turning left. Use the right lane for slower speeds, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your car. What should you expect?

options.text: Honk your horn.
The child will have total control of the bicycle.
The unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: The unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and may make sudden turns without warning. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the truck driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in the mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the truck stops quickly.

questions.question: Before you stop your car at a traffic signal or sign, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for other traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for other traffic.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to be aware of traffic around you. Release the accelerator and move your foot to the brake. Brake with steady, even pressure for a smooth stop.

questions.question: Your car's rear end is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel to the left.
Turn the steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, release the accelerator and brake gently. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding. If you have anti-lock brakes, brake firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if traffic lights favor the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your car. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: A broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line. When is passing allowed?

options.text: From the side next to the solid yellow line.
From neither direction.
From the side next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the side next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. Passing is not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycles on the road?

options.text: They have the same rights and responsibilities as other motor vehicles.
They do not follow traffic rules.
They must always yield to larger motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have the same rights and responsibilities as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the same rights and responsibilities as other motor vehicles. Other drivers should respect their rights on the road.

questions.question: When should you slow down before a curve?

options.text: Before you enter the curve.
After you finish the curve.
In the middle of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Driving too fast around a curve can cause your tires to lose grip on the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs warn you about school zones. Watch for children and obey the speed limit in school zones.
